Your daily calorie and macro targets are set by AI. When you tap Recalculate Goals, or automatically about once a week if Adaptive Goals is on, Chompass sends your profile, the reference equations below, your recently logged food, and your weight trend to your AI provider. It starts from these peer-reviewed formulas, then adjusts them to your data to estimate your maintenance and targets.
Default formula for resting metabolism. Used when you haven\'t entered a body fat %.
Used automatically when you\'ve entered a body fat %. More accurate for lean and athletic users since it derives BMR from lean body mass instead of total weight.

TDEE = BMR × activity multiplier. The multiplier corresponds to your selected activity level. Moderate uses 1.465 (between FAO/WHO light 1.375 and moderate 1.55) for desk-active users who exercise a few times per week. This is the maintenance baseline the AI starts from (unless Energy Burn supplies a measured one).
Sedentary: 1.2 · Light: 1.375 · Moderate: 1.465 · Active: 1.55 · Very Active: 1.725 · Extra Active: 1.9
Active burn on the home ring

Home Display lets you add active burn to your goal, track net intake, or show a burn hint. Your activity-level estimate is TDEE minus BMR (the PAL multiplier portion). Add Active and Dual use that estimate when Health Connect is off; Net requires measured Health Connect burn. Add Active splits your stored goal into a sedentary base plus today\'s active layer so activity is not counted twice. With Add Active, set Activity Level to everyday non-training life; measured or estimated active covers workouts so they are not stacked on a high PAL.
estimated active = TDEE − BMR\nsedentary budget = calorie goal − estimated active\nAdd Active goal = sedentary budget + (measured or estimated active)

Maintenance starts from your TDEE. With Energy Burn on, it starts from your measured Health Connect burn (a 14-day Active + Basal average) instead. The AI refines maintenance against your logged intake and weight trend, then applies your goal: a weekly weight-change rate becomes a daily calorie deficit (Lose) or surplus (Gain).
1 lb of body fat ≈ 3,500 kcal · 1 kg ≈ 7,700 kcal\nYour weekly rate ÷ 7 is subtracted from (Lose) or added to (Gain) maintenance to set the daily calorie target.

The AI fits protein, carbs, and fat to your calorie target, using these references as a guide. Protein scales with your activity level (and is based on lean body mass when a body fat %% is set); fat is set from bodyweight; carbs fill the rest. You can lock any value or edit it yourself in Settings.
Protein: ~0.8-2.2 g per kg by activity level (raised slightly when losing)\nFat: ~0.6 g per kg bodyweight\nCarbs: remaining calories ÷ 4 kcal/g

Calorie, macro, fiber, sugar, saturated fat, cholesterol, sodium, potassium and other micronutrient values returned per meal are AI-generated estimates from the food image, voice transcript, or text description, using the AI provider you selected.

Progress charts and goal ETA use your recent food logs and weigh-ins (up to 90 days). When you log on fewer than half the days in the window, intake is averaged across calendar days so occasional big-log days do not inflate the forecast. Otherwise intake is averaged across logged days only. Observed weight trend uses a robust median-slope (Theil–Sen) fit on scale entries.
predicted kg/week = (avgDailyCalories − TDEE) × 7 ÷ 7,700\nobserved kg/week = Theil–Sen slope × 7\nsparse logging: avg intake ÷ calendar days when logged days < 50%% of window

When enabled, Chompass compares your observed weight trend to your selected weekly pace and nudges calories by up to ±150 kcal/day (minimum 25 kcal change). Safety floor: max(BMR, 1,200 kcal). Safety ceiling: 125%% of measured or formula maintenance. Requires at least 4 logged food days and 3 weigh-ins, or Health Connect energy data.

Optional circumferences can derive waist-to-hip, waist-to-height, US Navy body-fat %, and wrist frame size. These are rough tape-measure estimates. They do not override BMR unless you separately enter a body-fat percentage on your profile.
Waist-to-hip = waist ÷ hips\nWaist-to-height = waist ÷ height\nUS Navy %BF: sex-specific log equations (neck, waist, hips, height)

Chompass is an estimation tool, not a clinical instrument. Formula estimates can be off (often around ±10%% for BMR). Consult a registered dietitian, physician, or sports medicine professional before significant diet changes, especially if you have a medical condition, are pregnant or breastfeeding, are under 18, or are managing an eating disorder.
Read this before making major diet changes
Chompass helps you track food and weight, but it is not a medical device and it is not a replacement for care from a doctor, therapist, or dietitian.
If you are planning major diet or body-composition changes, talk to a doctor or dietitian first so your plan fits your health history.
If you have a current or past eating disorder, or tracking starts increasing anxiety around food or body image, pause app use and speak with your care team.

Low body-fat caution: staying very lean for long periods can carry risk. In women, very low body fat can affect hormonal and menstrual health. In men, very low body fat can affect hormones, mood, recovery, and performance.
If you notice fatigue, dizziness, sleep disruption, mood changes, menstrual changes, or reduced libido, get medical advice promptly.
Hydration goals and drink reminders are estimates, not medical advice. They never replace thirst or guidance from your doctor. Drink enough even when the app does not remind you.

Chompass is a tracking helper, not a clinical tool. If you have a history of disordered eating, or tracking increases stress around food or body image, pause and talk with a doctor or therapist before continuing.
Low body-fat caution: staying too lean for too long can affect hormones, recovery, and overall health in both women and men.

This is not medical advice. Formula estimates can be off. Consult a registered dietitian, physician, or sports medicine professional before significant diet changes, especially if you have a medical condition, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or are under 18.

Photo estimates and vague quantity labels (handful, cup, serving) are often inaccurate. App suggestions and especially AI/LLM output are estimates only, not medical facts. Verify important numbers yourself.

“What if?” meal impact, including today’s logged diary totals
Coach chat, including your profile and recent logs
Your profile when AI estimates goals (plan, recalculate, adaptive goals)
